transcript_body:
Meeting header: 2026-03-19 16:00 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Chen (Redwood SE), Ravi Kapoor (Redwood Partnerships), Lena Rodriguez (Odyssey), Marco DiStefano (Odyssey), Dr. Anil Kumar (Odyssey), Sofia Nguyen (Odyssey)

Summary: quick intro, goal to explore partner/reseller and technical integration for Odyssey's GPU platform into Redwood's Dedicated/Private offerings, surface blockers (networking, data residency, certs), and agree next steps.

[00:00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, super excited to meet the Odyssey team. Quick round robin?
[00:00:07] Lena (Odyssey): Hi, Lena here, head of partnerships. We run partner GTM for Odyssey, we provide GPU infra and managed clusters.
[00:00:12] Marco (Odyssey): Marco, business dev, looking at reseller and channel ops.
[00:00:16] Anil (Odyssey): Anil, lead architect, I'll focus on how the tech will integrate.
[00:00:20] Ethan (Redwood): Ethan, SE at Redwood, I'll cover the integration and benchmarks.
[00:00:25] Maya: Great, high level agenda: 1) partner models, 2) high-level architecture options, 3) security/compliance, 4) bench/ops and next steps.

[00:02:03] Lena: From Odyssey side, we want to offer customers more out-of-the-box LLM inference. We think partnering with Redwood gives customers the runtime + control without Odyssey having to build inference stack. Interested in resale & managed offering.
[00:02:15] Marco: Also curious about revenue split, support ownership, and lead routing.

[00:03:40] Maya: Totally. We do hosted API for quick starts, Dedicated reserved pools for predictable throughput, and Private (VPC/on-prem) for regulated customers. For channel partners, we've seen both reseller and co-sell models work.
[00:03:55] Ravi (Redwood): On pricing we can surface a partner discount + referral commission. We'll need to align on SLAs for Dedicated/private engagements.

[00:05:10] Anil: On the private side, how does Redwood handle network connectivity? VPC peering or customer-managed infra?
[00:05:22] Ethan: We support a private control plane with customer-managed networking. Typical patterns: VPC peering or private link, and for on-prem we ship a package. There are some slight differences in cert management and key mgmt.
[00:05:30] Speaker 1: (inaudible) private control plane sometimes read as private plane.

[00:06:45] Marco: Are there limitations on models or quantization when running in Dedicated vs Private?
[00:06:52] Ethan: Functionally both support same model catalog but Dedicated/Private gives you more control over hardware and driver versions which affects kernel selection. Quantized kernels require specific runtimes on the host. Sometimes terms get mis-said as "q-ization kernels" in docs.

[00:08:12] Lena: Security questions: we have enterprise customers that require SOC2, SSO integration, and KMS. Does Redwood integrate with external KMS/HSM?
[00:08:20] Maya: Yes, we support KMS integrations and can integrate customer KMS for Private. We have SOC2 compliance and audit logs, and SSO via SAML/Okta. We'll share security docs.

[00:09:40] Anil: For audit logs, is there an option to ship logs to customer SIEM?
[00:09:46] Ethan: Yes, export hooks or SIEM forwarding, and retention is configurable.

[00:11:05] Anil: Network latency is a big focus. Typical customers want <50ms for chat workloads. Can Redwood meet that on Odyssey hardware?
[00:11:15] Ethan: Latency depends on model family and sequence length. With our runtime optimizations (attention kernels, KV cache, continuous batching), on-prem/colocated Dedicated pools can hit low latency. We'll need a benchmark with your hardware and model sizes.
[00:11:28] Speaker 2: kernel selecshun comes up often (transcription quirk).

[00:12:40] Marco: For co-selling, how do leads get routed and what are expectations for support SLAs?
[00:12:48] Ravi: Usually partner refers and we own initial onboarding, then joint support for Dedicated accounts. SLAs are part of the partner agreement.

[00:14:02] Lena: On the integration side, operationally what does Odyssey need to do to onboard customers to Redwood's Dedicated?
[00:14:10] Ethan: High level: 1) set up network connectivity (VPC peering/private link), 2) configure auth/SSO and KMS, 3) choose model variants and quantization profiles, 4) run benchmarks to set autoscale and batching policies. We'll provide a checklist.

[00:16:35] Anil: Regarding model variants and fallbacks, you mentioned automatic fallback to compatible model variants when capacity constrained. How deterministic is that?
[00:16:45] Ethan: We use policy-based routing\u2014latency or cost policies. Fallback is configurable per-route so you can say prefer exact model or allow close family. Docs call it smart routing, sometimes transcribed as "smart routing or fall back".

[00:18:00] Marco: Commercially, how do we price the bundle? Do we bill customers through Odyssey or Redwood?
[00:18:08] Maya: Both are possible. Reseller model usually bills through partner with partner margin. Co-sell customers can have joint invoices or be billed on Redwood with revenue share. We'll send templates.

[00:19:40] Lena: Are there any enterprise customers you have that would be similar references?
[00:19:46] Maya: We can share references once NDA is in place; we have a few mid-market and enterprise accounts using Dedicated and Private for regulated workloads.

[00:21:15] Anil: On quantization: we often want 4-bit quantized models to save GPU mem. Any caveats?
[00:21:22] Ethan: 4-bit works but depends on kernel support and model family. We recommend a validation pass\u2014sometimes quality drops for certain tasks. Redwood Optimize offers quant recommendation by workload. We'll share some evals.

[00:22:40] Lena: Operational question: who handles incident response for customer-facing outages?
[00:22:46] Maya: Depends on the agreement. For Dedicated we typically provide platform support; for Private it's customer-managed with Redwood on-call for platform issues per SLA. Severity escalation matrix will be in the SOW.

[00:24:10] Marco: Any IP or data residency concerns? Some of our customers need data never leave region.
[00:24:18] Ethan: Private deployment/region pinning + KMS lets you keep data in-region. For Hosted we have region options but privacy and residency requirements typically push customers to Private or Dedicated in-region.

[00:25:40] Anil: Is there support for GPU telemetry and utilization dashboards we can integrate into Odyssey's console?
[00:25:48] Ethan: Yes, Redwood Console exposes token-level costs, per-route model dashboards, and we can export metrics to your monitoring system. We'll point to APIs for that.

[00:27:05] Speaker 3: (small cross-talk)

[00:27:40] Maya: On the partner ops side, let's map initial pilot requirements: small set of customers, run benchmarks, define SLA, then roll into reseller co-sell. Does that sound right?
[00:27:50] Lena: Yes, pilot first. We'll identify 2-3 customers for initial pilot.

[00:29:10] Marco: Timeline: if we move quick, can we do pilot in 4-6 weeks?
[00:29:17] Ethan: Yes, assuming we get sample workloads and access, we can run initial bench in 1-2 weeks and a pilot within 4-6 weeks.

[00:30:40] Anil: Benchmarks: what metrics do you need from us? QPS, typical seq len, model family, concurrency, and desired p50/p95 latency targets.
[00:30:50] Ethan: Exactly. Also whether customers prefer small context windows (chat) or long-form generation. Send a sample prompt set if possible.

[00:32:15] Lena: For go-to-market, we'd like co-branded collateral and enablement.
[00:32:22] Maya: We'll provide partner one-pager, technical onboarding deck, and sales play.

[00:34:00] Marco: Any compliance notes: SOC2 scope and attestation cadence?
[00:34:07] Ravi: We are SOC2 Type II, annual attestation; we can provide AOC and scoping docs.

[00:35:30] Anil: A couple of low-level items: is there an agent or sidecar for routing traffic to Dedicated pools, or is it control-plane only?
[00:35:38] Ethan: Mostly control-plane, but for some edge/topology patterns we use a small routing agent. We can document network ports and certs.

[00:36:50] Lena: Are there onboarding fees for partners?
[00:36:55] Maya: Typically none for basic enablement; enterprise integrations may have SOW fees for private deployments. We'll outline in partner docs.

[00:38:30] Sofia (Odyssey): Curious about support handoff — level 1 handled by Odyssey?
[00:38:36] Ravi: Partner support tiers vary; we can design a joint-support flow.

[00:40:05] Marco: Let's talk about next steps quickly.
[00:40:10] Maya: Action items: I'll send partner/reseller deck and draft terms; Ethan will assemble tech integration doc and a benchmark template; Anil will share workload samples; Lena will confirm pilot customers and internal owners.

[00:42:20] Lena: Sounds good. One last ask: can you share a sample latency/cost spreadsheet so we can model pricing for customers?
[00:42:28] Maya: Yes we'll share a benchmark/cost model and request your hardware profile.

[00:44:00] Anil: Any blockers from Redwood's side before we go deeper?
[00:44:06] Maya: None major; need to align on NDA/partner terms and schedule the deep tech call.

[00:45:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and docs. Next meeting: technical deep dive tentatively week of 2026-03-23.
[00:46:00] Marco: Thanks all.
[00:46:05] Ethan: Thanks, talk soon.

Recap / Action items (auto-generated):
- Maya Patel: Send partner deck + draft reseller terms (due 2026-03-23)
- Ethan Chen: Tech integration doc (VPC/peering, KMS, certs) + benchmark template (due 2026-03-25)
- Anil Kumar: Share sample workload and target SLAs (due 2026-03-24)

References mentioned: partner deck (link to be shared), security docs (SOC2 AOC), sample benchmarks spreadsheet.

Notes on transcription quality: medium - several names and technical terms were slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "kernel selection" -> "kernel selecshun", "KV cache" -> "KV cash").
